newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals tumble by close on Swiss move.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals tumble by close on Swiss move.

text.p: New York precious metals ended sharply lower Friday as the specter of Swiss gold sales continued to dog market sentiment, traders said.
"Gold has suffered from this big dent to sentiment of having the Swiss turning on them -- it's almost like betrayal," Dinsa Mehta of Chase Manhattan said.
Bullion fell below the psychological level of $350.00 an ounce to $348.30/80 an ounce.
COMEX April gold settled down $3.70 at $349.90, traded $353.50 to $349.10. Volume was estimated at 68,000 lots.
Floor sources said April gold needed to stay above $349.10 to $349.40 to avoid triggering heavy sell stops.
Switzerland said earlier this week it planned to sell 40 tonnes of gold over 10 years to raise cash for victims of the Holocaust and other tragedies.

Mehta said although the deal legitimized sales of gold reserves by central banks, it still looked uncertain because the Swiss parliament has yet to vote on it, and the selloff would take place over a long period.
"But the larger point is still that even the purists are willing to talk about selling gold," Mehta added.
COMEX May silver settled 4.2 cents lower at $5.185, traded $5.23 to $5.165. Volume was estimated at 17,000 lots.
NYMEX platinum futures ended down sharply, with April delivery settling $7.80 lower at $378.50.
Some dealers said the drop was due to fading threat of a strike at Norilsk in Russia, one of the world's biggest producers of the metal.
But others said that after platinum's rapid advance in recent weeks, some sort of pullback was inevitable.
"The strike has been discounted by the market already and this was just a technical correction," a market player said. "I would look for it to dip to a low of $370.00 and then go back up to $400."
June NYMEX palladium went out $1.25 lower at $150.75.
